title: Cedarview - Hosted API embeddings + rerank walkthrough
meeting_header: Date: 2026-11-04 | Time: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Ross (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood CSM); Liam O'Connell, Sara Kim, Amir Patel, Nora Li (Cedarview)
summary: Hosted API demo focused on embeddings + reranking pipeline for product search. Reviewed Redwood embeddings endpoints, two-stage retrieval + rerank flow, cost/latency tradeoffs, and Redwood Console monitoring and Optimize suggestions. Customer concerned about PII, data residency, and evaluation metrics; agreed next steps to share pilot pricing, security pack, and a demo notebook with benchmark scripts.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood — I'll kick us off. Can folks state names quickly?
[00:08] Liam O'Connell: Liam here, Head of Search at Cedarview.
[00:11] Sara Kim: Sara, ML engineer.
[00:13] Amir Patel: Amir, CTO.
[00:16] Nora Li: Nora, product.
[00:18] Maya Chen: Great, Ethan's our SE, he'll run the demo, and Priya will handle follow ups.
[00:25] Ethan Ross: Hey all — quick agenda: show hosted embeddings and rerank endpoints, demo a two-stage pipeline, peek at Console/Optimize, then Q&A. Anything to add?
[00:34] Liam O'Connell: We're mostly interested in improving product search relevance across web and mobile, and the cost is a hard constraint.
[00:39] Maya Chen: Perfect.
[00:42] Ethan Ross: Ok jumping in — first slide, the hosted embeddings endpoint: single REST call to /v1/embeddings, supports batched inputs, returns 1536-d vectors (depends on model). For Cedarview we'd pick a small-ish embed model to balance cost with recall.
[01:05] Sara Kim: Quick Q: do you persist embeddings on your side? We want to keep vector storage on our infra, not Redwood.
[01:12] Ethan Ross: Yes, hosted inference only — we don't persist your document vectors unless you opt into our managed embeddings store. Most customers store vectors in Pinecone, FAISS, or Weaviate on their side.
[01:25] Amir Patel: Are there pre-built exports to Pinecone?
[01:28] Ethan Ross: We have example notebooks for Pinecone and Weaviate; I'll share links after the call. (link: https://redwood.example.com/notebooks/embeddings-to-pinecone)
[01:35] Liam O'Connell: Cool. Also curious about rerank — how does that integrate?
[01:39] Ethan Ross: Rerank is a hosted scoring endpoint; typical flow: first stage retrieve top-K from your vector DB, second stage call Redwood's /v1/rerank with query + candidate docs (text or short context) and we return scores and reordered list. That allows you to use a cheaper embed model for retrieval and a stronger reranker for final sort.
[01:58] Nora Li: Does rerank return explanations or token-level highlights?
[02:02] Ethan Ross: We return scores and optional structured outputs if you use templating/function calling. Not full token alignments — it's more of a relevance score plus metadata.
[02:12] Sara Kim: Latency numbers? We're targeting 200ms p95 for mobile queries.
[02:18] Ethan Ross: For single-shot rerank with 10 candidates, hosted in our US region, typical p95 is 80-200ms depending on model and sequence length. We can get to 200ms p95 with mid-size rerank models. If you need lower latency we can recommend model variants or dedicated capacity.
[02:35] Liam O'Connell: And cost per request ballpark?
[02:38] Ethan Ross: It varies: embeddings cheap per 1k tokens, rerank measured per call plus tokens. I'll include sample cost estimates in the follow up.
[02:46] Maya Chen: Also note Redwood Optimize will suggest batching, prefix caching, and quantized model variants — that usually moves the needle on cost.
[02:56] Amir Patel: Data residency / PII — our product descriptions contain customer PII sometimes. We need encryption at rest, KMS, and SOC2.
[03:05] Priya Kapoor: We have SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, and KMS integrations. For Private deployments we support VPC and on-prem. For hosted we can do customer-managed key via KMS in certain plans. I'll attach our security pack.
[03:18] Liam O'Connell: Is there an audit log we can ship to Splunk?
[03:22] Ethan Ross: Yes, audit logs and usage traces can be exported; Console has per-token breakdowns and trace hooks you can pipe to SIEM.
[03:31] Ethan Ross: Moving to live demo — I'm sharing screen.
[03:35] [screen-share noise]
[03:40] Ethan Ross: Here is the Console route for embeddings, you can create API keys, see per-route latency, and set rate limits. I'll run a sample query: sending 5 product titles as a batch to /v1/embeddings now.
[03:55] [typing sounds]
[04:02] Ethan Ross: Response: vectors returned, you see timing breakdown — tokenization 4ms, model 23ms, overhead 6ms.
[04:12] Nora Li: That timing breakdown is super helpful.
[04:15] Ethan Ross: Now for rerank example — we fetched 10 candidates from a FAISS index (local for demo) and call /v1/rerank with query plus the 10 snippets.
[04:30] Ethan Ross: Demo returns reordered list with scores. Watch the Console traces — you can see model used, input tokens, and cost estimate.
[04:44] Sara Kim: On the two-stage flow — do you have recommendations for K (retrieval size) vs latency?
[04:50] Ethan Ross: Typical pattern: K=50 for recall, then rerank top 10 locally. But for tight latency budgets you can do K=20 and stronger reranker. Optimize offers suggestions by analyzing query length histograms and recommending K and batching thresholds.
[05:05] Liam O'Connell: What about caching? Many queries repeat.
[05:08] Ethan Ross: We support prefix/KV caching built into the runtime. For product search if top queries are repetitive you can cache embeddings or rerank outputs. Cache hit rates can cut costs substantially.
[05:20] Amir Patel: How do we evaluate improvements? We track MRR and NDCG at 10 and conversion lift.
[05:27] Ethan Ross: That's aligned — we can run an A/B via the Console rollouts and track metric deltas against your eval set. Bring us a labeled dev set, we run evals and produce NDCG/MRR comparisons.
[05:41] Sara Kim: Could we run a small benchmark — 5k queries — to compare our current pipeline vs Redwood hosted rerank?
[05:47] Maya Chen: Absolutely, that sounds like a pilot. Typical pilot: 4 weeks, 5k queries/day or a representative sample, Redwood supplies the rerank endpoint and benchmarking notebook, you host vectors.
[05:57] Nora Li: Timeline — how quickly could we start?
[06:00] Maya Chen: We can spin pilot in 1 week once NDA/po signed and keys provisioned.
[06:06] Liam O'Connell: Any blockers for us? We need to confirm data residency and whether using hosted means data leaves EU.
[06:13] Priya Kapoor: We have EU regions and can pin routes to region; if strict residency is required we recommend Private deployment. We'll surface options in the security pack.
[06:24] [10:00-ish skip — demo continues, some background chatter]
[10:02] Ethan Ross: Switching to Console Optimize tab — here's a suggested config: use medium embed for ingest, store in your vector DB, retrieve top 40, rerank top 8, enable caching with 24h TTL for high frequency queries, quantize reranker to int8 for throughput.
[10:21] Liam O'Connell: Quantization — do you see major quality regressions?
[10:24] Ethan Ross: Usually small. We run automated evals on your test set and flag drops beyond your tolerance. You can also A/B with graceful fallbacks to unquantized if quality drops.
[10:35] Sara Kim: Can we host model weights ourselves and only use Redwood control plane?
[10:39] Ethan Ross: That's our Private deployment model — bring-your-own weights in on-prem is supported with dedicated control plane. For hosted, weights are managed by Redwood.
[10:48] Amir Patel: Security pack and SOC docs please.
[10:50] Priya Kapoor: I'll attach SOC2 report and our KMS integration guide.
[11:00] Nora Li: About cost — can you give a worked example around 1M queries/month?
[11:05] Maya Chen: We'll produce a price sheet with assumptions: avg tokens per query, embedding calls per query, rerank calls per user session. I'll include a few scenarios (conservative, optimized).
[11:17] Ethan Ross: Also flagging competitors — some customers compare us to Pinecone for vector DB, and to managed endpoints on cloud vendors; we differentiate on unified rerank + console insights.
[11:29] Liam O'Connell: We use Pinecone already. How seamless is integration?
[11:33] Ethan Ross: There's a one-liner in the notebook to push embeddings to Pinecone; retrieval and rerank are standard.
[11:39] [slight crosstalk]
[15:00] Ethan Ross: Demo notebook repo link: https://redwood.example.com/repos/cedarview-demo (I'll post in follow-up).
[15:10] Nora Li: Could you include an example showing full trace of a query to link Console metrics to our APM?
[15:15] Ethan Ross: Yes, we can include trace hooks for Datadog/Zipkin.
[15:22] Sara Kim: One more on ranking metrics — do you support click-model calibration?
[15:27] Ethan Ross: We don't do click log collection for you, but we can run evaluation harnesses on your labeled data and also accept click logs if you want us to transform them to training/eval sets under a pilot agreement.
[15:40] Liam O'Connell: Who's my point of contact for SSO and provisioning?
[15:44] Maya Chen: Priya will manage provisioning and SSO (SAML).
[15:48] Priya Kapoor: I'll reach out to your IT with our SSO docs and a provisioning checklist.
[16:00] [wrap-up]
[16:02] Maya Chen: Recap: pilot proposal (4 weeks) — Redwood provides hosted rerank endpoints and a demo notebook; Cedarview hosts vectors; evaluation on NDCG/MRR; security pack and pricing sent.
[16:14] Liam O'Connell: Sounds good.
[16:16] Amir Patel: One ask — put a note about retention policies; we store logs for 90 days but want control.
[16:22] Priya Kapoor: We can configure retention per-customer; I'll include options (30/90/365 days).
[16:28] Maya Chen: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the materials and proposed pilot contract.
[16:34] [meeting ends]
